name: navigator-scan-permission-decision
body:
Decision record for the navigator-scan-permission change-set.

SOURCE / DECISION (user's decision). Today the distributed `codebase-navigator` prompt holds `apg_scan: allow` AND carries a bespoke scan-consent ritual: non-negotiable rule 7 ("ask the user first (via the `question` tool)"; "Only run `apg_scan` after they approve"), the "### Scanning a project" intro ("ask the user before running a scan … never kick one off unprompted"), the "When a scan is needed" step 0, the query-patterns table row ("ask the user first — scans can be lengthy"), the "gate for every answer" bullet, and the Implementation-flow cadence ("you run scans (after user approval)" / step 3 "(after user approval)"). The user chose to STOP asking for consent in the guidance and instead make the permission `apg_scan: ask` — opencode then prompts natively when the tool is called, and the user may choose "always allow". Net: no bespoke consent ritual; the permission layer is the gate.

RESOLUTION. Added `requirements.user.navigator-agent` (pre-existing coordinator actor — reused) ⊃ `requirements.requirement.navigator-scan-permission`, the domain entity `domain.entity.scan-authorization` (scan consent delegated to opencode's per-call permission prompt, with an always-allow escape), and the narrow branch-added solution component `solution.component.navigator-scan-permission-coherence-test`. Spine: user ⊃ requirement —drives→ entity —realised-by→ {`solution.component.codebase-navigator-prompt` (REUSED, already implemented-by the prompt file), `solution.component.navigator-scan-permission-coherence-test` (NEW)} —implemented-by→ {`opencode-suite/agents/codebase-navigator.md`, `rust.main_e2e.e2e.coordinator_agent_carries_review_action_and_dispatch_prose`}. Both implemented-by targets RESOLVE in the branch graph, so no planned Implementation node is authored here (that is the plan-writer's job if it chooses otherwise). Added the law `requirements.constraint.scan-consent-via-permission` attaches-to the requirement. [with user — the approach was the user's explicit decision]

TEST OWNER CHOICE. The test edit is a `modifies` over the EXISTING test fn `rust.main_e2e.e2e.coordinator_agent_carries_review_action_and_dispatch_prose` (resolves, `tests/main_e2e.rs:2148-2266`, `code_type = 'test'`), anchored through the NEW narrow component. The prior `solution.component.navigator-isolation-coherence-test` already implemented-by the same fn; it is pre-existing/not branch-added (exempt from coverage) and reusing it would leave this test edit uncovered, so a new narrow component is used and the prior component's edge is left intact. Overlapping implemented-by ownership is established practice. The fn name is deliberately unchanged (no new test fn: a new fn's FQN would not resolve and cannot be the target of an implemented-by edge). [autonomous]

PROMPT OWNER CHOICE. Reused `solution.component.codebase-navigator-prompt` for the prompt file rather than minting a new component — it owns the prompt file 1:1 and this change-set edits that same file, so its implemented-by set stays exactly the edited file. [autonomous]

LEFT AS-IS (historical / other concerns). `requirements.constraint.navigator-cadence-stated` and `requirements.note.navigator-task-cadence-decision` mention "a scan (after user approval)" as part of the per-task cadence decision record; they are left untouched as historical records of the prior change-set, since this change-set does not edit the cadence prose beyond the two scan-approval clauses named in the requirement. No other `opencode-suite/agents/*` file is edited; the repo's own `.opencode/agents/**` are consumer artifacts and are never edited. No binary behaviour change.
